raw_response:
I farm small land and I am already 72, so I will keep the plan steady and familiar instead of chasing anything complicated. On my 6 mu, I will put 4 mu into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my land use and fits Quzhou well, especially since I have well irrigation and long experience with it. I will keep cotton on 2 mu, not more, because cotton takes more hand work and more pest watching, and with only two people in the household I do not want too much labor pressure. I will use better seed on all three crops because on such a small area I care more about stable stand and stable yield than saving a little on seed. I will fertilize at moderate rates, not too heavily, because I want dependable output and I know excessive fertilizer can waste money and create weak growth. I will irrigate wheat and maize according to their key water periods, and I will give cotton somewhat more attention because it stays longer in the field. I will keep tillage simple and practical: rotary for wheat land preparation, no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save labor and catch the season, and plough for cotton ground so the soil is looser at the start. My goal this year is not maximum output at all cost; it is stable grain, manageable labor, and a cotton area small enough that I can still handle it carefully.
